title: Allentown Home Rebates 2026: PPL Electric Heat Pump, Insulation and Appliance Offers
desc: Allentown home rebates in 2026: PPL Electric pays $225 to $500 for heat pumps, $400 for a heat pump water heater, up to $500 for insulation, plus thermostat and appliance offers.
lead: PPL Electric's rebates fit Allentown well. About 39.5% of households heat with electricity and 14.1% with fuel oil, which are the homes that save most by switching to a heat pump, and PPL pays for heat pumps, a heat pump water heater, insulation, air sealing, a thermostat and several appliances. The federal credits ended in 2025. Here is what we read in PPL's rebate store on October 5, 2026.
cards_heading: What PPL Electric pays Allentown homes in 2026
cards_intro: PPL lists 15 rebates in its store, and each has an Apply for Rebate button. Some customers qualify for larger enhanced amounts based on income, which is why several cards show two numbers. Equipment installed on or before May 31, 2026 is no longer eligible.

cards.title: Air source heat pump
cards.note: ENERGY STAR certified, rated as a whole system in the AHRI database. Two efficiency tiers, from SEER2 15.2 and from SEER2 16.3.

cards.title: Mini-split and ground source heat pumps
cards.note: Mini-splits need SEER2 15.2+, EER2 11.7+ and HSPF2 7.8+. Ground source units need ENERGY STAR certification.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: ENERGY STAR certified with a UEF of 3.3 or higher.

cards.title: Smart thermostat
cards.note: Needs a heat pump, or fossil heat with central A/C, or an electric furnace with central A/C. Not for baseboard heat.

cards.title: Insulation and air sealing
cards.note: Attic, exterior wall, rim joist and basement wall, plus air sealing up to $150. Needs electric heat, or central A/C with non-electric heat.

cards.title: Appliances and cooling
cards.note: Refrigerator $50 or $75, dehumidifier $25 or $50, air purifier $25, central A/C $150 or $175, room A/C $15.

cards.title: Home battery
cards.note: None of PPL's 15 rebates is for a battery. See our state page for what to weigh instead.

cards.title: Penn Energy Savers
cards.note: The state's federal-funded rebates have no launch date or amounts yet.

cards.title: Weatherization Assistance Program
cards.note: For households at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, through your county's agency.

cards.title: Federal 25C and 25D credits
cards.note: Nothing for work done after December 31, 2025.

after_cards: All of PPL's offers are claimed in the same rebate store, so one account handles a heat pump, a thermostat and an insulation job in a single visit. The "Check Best Offers" questions sort you into the standard or enhanced level before you buy.
sections: The Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts 49,502 homes in Allentown, with 46,374 occupied. Rowhouses and twins are 36.0% of the stock, detached houses 25.9% and buildings of two to four units 15.0%. Homes are old: 82.1% were built before 1980 and 37.9% before 1940, with only 9.3% from 2000 or later.

Allentown is a renter city: 56.8% of households rent and 43.2% own, the highest rental share of the four Pennsylvania cities we cover. PPL pays the customer who buys the equipment, so many of these upgrades need a landlord. Tenants can still use the small ones: a thermostat on an eligible system, a dehumidifier, an air purifier or a refrigerator.

Fuel oil heats 14.1% of Allentown households, the highest oil share of our four cities, against 2.7% in Philadelphia and 0.6% in Pittsburgh. Oil costs more per unit of heat and needs deliveries, so a heat pump runs most of the season and the oil furnace can stay as backup. The PPL heat pump pages we read set no rule about the old fuel, only about the efficiency and rating of the new system.

Utility gas heats 44.2% of homes and electricity 39.5%. For electric homes, a heat pump cuts power use for the same warmth. For gas homes, savings are smaller, and a heat pump makes more sense when the central A/C needs replacing anyway. PPL's insulation and thermostat rebates also cover gas-heated homes, but only with central air conditioning.
Allentown's average January low is about -4.3°C (24°F), and the coldest reading in our ten years of data was -23.2°C. Ask for a cold-climate model and ask how the system handles the coldest nights.

PPL's income-based enhanced amounts are shown as "or" figures because the store does not tell us the rule behind each number. Use its Check Best Offers tool. We also did not read the county weatherization agency's page, so call the agency your county uses to apply.
installers_intro: Ranked by Google reviews (minimum five). We don't take referral fees or paid placements. Ask for the AHRI certificate that lists the whole system, because PPL does not accept ratings for single parts.
claim_steps: Run PPL's Check Best Offers questions before you buy.
Check that your heating and cooling setup fits the rule for the item you want.
Get quotes that list model numbers, and ask for the AHRI certificate on a heat pump.
Keep the paid invoice, and the labor invoice for insulation and thermostats.
Apply in PPL's rebate store, and check the deadline it shows.
faq: How much does PPL pay for a heat pump in Allentown?
$225 or $325 for an air source heat pump, $225 for a mini-split and $500 for a ground source heat pump, all ENERGY STAR certified.

Yes. Up to $200 or $500 each for attic, exterior wall, rim joist and basement wall insulation, and up to $150 for air sealing. The space must be conditioned by electric heat, or by central A/C if the heat is not electric.
Can I claim a heat pump I installed last spring?
No. PPL says equipment installed on or before May 31, 2026 is no longer eligible.
Is there a PPL rebate for a battery or solar?
No. PPL's 15 rebates cover heat pumps, a heat pump water heater, a thermostat, insulation, air sealing, appliances and air conditioners. None is for a battery or solar.
Is the federal tax credit still available?
No. The federal credits for heat pumps, insulation, solar and batteries ended for spending after December 31, 2025.
